use_case: Revenue-management pricing (SYS-13): machine-learning demand forecasts and daily rate recommendations. Rates publish automatically to SYS-01, the booking engine, and the channel manager for Resorts 1 and 2; Hotels 3 to 6 receive recommendations that the Director of Revenue Management enters in the brand system
vendor_or_model: Revenue-management vendor (machine-learning forecasting and pricing SaaS)
data_categories: Aggregated bookings and stay history from the nightly SYS-01 and SYS-02 extracts; public competitor rates; event calendars. The extract also carries guest names, which the model does not need (being removed)
affects_individuals: Yes (prices paid by about 147,000 stays a year; not individualized)
consequential_decision_category: None (room prices are not a listed consequential decision); treated as High during a declared state of emergency
human_in_the_loop: Today none at the resorts: rates publish automatically. Conditions: floor, ceiling, and 10% daily change limits; Director of Revenue Management approval outside them and for every increase during a declared emergency
applicable_laws: FTC Act Section 5 (15 U.S.C. 45(a), (n)); 16 CFR 464.2 (total price, including the $40 resort fee, in every display and channel feed); Fla. Stat. 501.160 (unconscionable prices in a declared state of emergency); Sherman Act 15 U.S.C. 1 litigation risk from pooled non-public data
status: In production since 2024; approved with conditions (due 2026-10-31)

use_case: Guest chatbot (SYS-14) on the resort websites and text messaging: answers questions, quotes availability and rates, and links to the booking engine
business_owner: Vice President of Sales and Marketing
vendor_or_model: Chatbot vendor (generative AI language model SaaS) with a company-built integration in the workloads account that reads SYS-01 availability and rates
data_categories: Guest questions, names, phone numbers, and emails; transcripts; availability and rates. Guests sometimes type card numbers (61 transcripts found)
human_in_the_loop: Staff handoff for booking changes, complaints, accessibility, medical, and hurricane questions; staff review 50 transcripts a week
applicable_laws: 16 CFR 464.2 and 464.3 (total price; fee descriptions); FTC Act Section 5 (accuracy of answers); PCI DSS v4.0.1 3.2.1 and 4.2.2 (card numbers in chat; N72-R01); Fla. Stat. 501.171 (transcripts with personal information; the vendor is a third-party agent)
status: In production since 2025-11; approved with conditions (due 2026-10-31)

use_case: CRO call recording with AI transcription and quality scoring (SYS-15): records about 900 calls a day, transcribes them, and scores agent calls against the CRO quality checklist
vendor_or_model: Contact center platform vendor (speech-to-text and scoring models; model provider carved out); recordings and transcripts stored in the workloads account
data_categories: Call audio of guests, callers, and 22 CRO agents; transcripts; quality scores. Recordings and transcripts hold spoken card numbers and security codes today
consequential_decision_category: None directly; quality scores are 1 of 4 inputs to the quarterly CRO incentive. Re-tier to High (Employment) if scores are used for discipline, termination, or scheduling
human_in_the_loop: Supervisors review every score before it is used for coaching or the incentive; agents can dispute a score
applicable_laws: Fla. Stat. 934.03(2)(d) (all parties' prior consent to interception); PCI DSS v4.0.1 3.3.1 and 3.3.1.2 (no security codes kept after authorization; N72-R01); Fla. Stat. 501.171 (card numbers with security codes are personal information); FTC Act Section 5
status: In production since 2025-03; approved with conditions (due 2026-12-31)

use_case: Applicant screening in the applicant tracking system (SYS-16): scores applications against job requirements and, until 2026-09-15, automatically declined applicants below a score threshold for hourly roles
vendor_or_model: Applicant tracking vendor's AI screening module (machine-learning ranking model)
data_categories: Applications and resumes (about 9,500 a year); screening answers; scores; voluntary EEO self-identification held separately for reporting
human_in_the_loop: Since 2026-09-15 automatic declines are off: a recruiter reviews every application the tool scores low before any decision; accommodation requests go to the HR Director
applicable_laws: Title VII disparate impact, 42 U.S.C. 2000e-2(k)(1)(A); ADA screening criteria, 42 U.S.C. 12112(b)(6); Uniform Guidelines on Employee Selection Procedures, 29 CFR 1607.4 (impact records; four-fifths rule of thumb); FTC Act Section 5 (vendor claims)
status: In production since 2025-06; conditional: automatic declines suspended; conditions due 2026-12-31 or retire

use_case: CCTV video analytics at the resorts (SYS-17): after-hours intrusion alerts for pools, beaches, and back-of-house doors; loitering and left-object alerts; people counting. A facial recognition feature is available but disabled
business_owner: Director of Loss Prevention and Safety
vendor_or_model: Video management software vendor (on-premises analytics models)
data_categories: Video of guests, visitors, and staff (30-day retention); alert snapshots; occupancy counts. No face templates while facial recognition stays disabled
consequential_decision_category: None while alerts only prompt a security officer to look; re-tier to High (Safety) if analytics replace patrols, and reassess before facial recognition is ever enabled
human_in_the_loop: Security officers review every alert on camera before acting; no guest is approached or removed on an alert alone
applicable_laws: FTC Act Section 5 (statements in the privacy notice and signage); Fla. Stat. 501.171(1)(g)1.a.(VI) and 501.702 (biometric data: whether face templates from video qualify is unsettled; counsel to confirm; treated as biometric data); Fla. Stat. 934.03 (no audio recording)
status: In production since 2024; approved with conditions (facial recognition locked by 2026-10-31)

use_case: Enterprise generative AI assistant (productivity suite add-on) for drafting, summarizing, and searching email and files
vendor_or_model: Enterprise generative AI assistant licensed with the productivity suite (tenant-bound; no training on company data under the contract)
data_categories: Whatever the user can already reach in email and files; Restricted card data must not be entered (POL-04 4.8)
human_in_the_loop: Users review every output before use (POL-05 4.10)
applicable_laws: PCI DSS v4.0.1 (card forms in mailboxes are searchable by the assistant until purged; N72-R01); FTC Act Section 5 (truthful marketing copy); POL-04 4.8; POL-05 4.10
status: Approved for 120 corporate users (security review 2026-06); expansion to hotels after the mailbox purge (POAM-013)
